dropped.claim: LCI Industries is a cyclical component supplier emerging from a severe downturn, with revenue recovering from $3.7B in 2024 to $4.1B in 2025 and operating margin improving to 6.8%. However, the business faces extreme concentration risk (33% of sales from two customers, 54% of OEM segment from RV trailers/fifth-wheels), acknowledged low barriers to entry, deteriorating cash conversion (operating cash flow fell from $602.5M in 2022 to $331.0M in 2025, now below net income), and material tariff/supply chain uncertainty (36% of materials imported, new worldwide tariffs effective February 2026). The company reversed three years of deleveraging by increasing long-term debt from $757.3M to $945.2M in 2025. While the Aftermarket segment (23% of sales, 34% of profit) provides some diversification, the core thesis depends on sustained RV market recovery and the ability to pass through volatile input costs in a low-barrier industry—both highly uncertain.

dropped.claim: LCI faces a toxic combination of extreme customer concentration (33% from two customers, no long-term contracts), acknowledged low barriers to entry, deteriorating cash conversion (operating cash flow now below net income), and material tariff/supply chain uncertainty affecting 36% of inputs. The company reversed deleveraging by increasing debt $187.9M in 2025 despite only modest revenue recovery, raising questions about capital allocation and organic growth quality. While the Aftermarket segment provides some diversification, the core OEM business (77% of sales) remains highly exposed to RV cyclicality, which drove revenue from $5.2B to $3.7B in two years. The acknowledged inability to fully pass through volatile steel and aluminum costs (40% of raw materials combined) in a low-barrier industry threatens margin sustainability. Management's claims of competitive advantages and high switching costs are undermined by their own admission that barriers to entry are generally low. The deteriorating cash conversion and debt increase during a recovery year suggest underlying business quality issues. This is a pass at current information density.
